title: Prenatal PM2.5 exposure drives epigenetic reprogramming of fetal macrophages linked to atopic dermatitis
task: Determine epigenetic mechanisms linking prenatal PM2.5 exposure to atopic dermatitis risk
key_results: First-trimester PM2.5 exposure causes FCER1G hypomethylation in fetal macrophages leading to sustained overexpression; elevated AD risk in early childhood; transcriptional program persists across developmental stages
comments: The multi-omics integration is comprehensive, but causality relies on correlative associations; experimental validation of PM2.5-induced epigenetic changes in human fetal tissues is limited.

title: Macrophages tune NK cell IFNγ production through direct lipid transfer

comments: The direct lipid transfer mechanism is well-characterized, but the physiological relevance to in vivo immune responses during infection or inflammation requires validation in pathologically relevant models.

hypotheses.hypothesis: CD36-mediated trogocytosis transfers fatty acids from macrophages to NK cells
hypotheses.result: Cell-cell contact required; CD36 protein transfer demonstrated via trogocytosis
